classification.text_en: The pen (qalam) is named in the Quran as the means by which God taught, and God swears by the pen and by what they write.

origin.note_en: The Quran does not describe how or when the pen was made.

purpose.text_en: God taught the human being by the pen what he did not know.

nature.note_en: The Quran does not describe the pen itself, its form or its material.

abilities.note_en: The Quran does not describe abilities of the pen beyond teaching by it and the writing of 'what they write'.

limitations.text_en: Pens and ink are small beside the words of God: if all the trees on the earth were pens, and the sea with seven more seas added to it were ink, the words of God would not run out.

relationship_with_humans.text_en: Humans learn by it: God taught the human being what he did not know, and the oath by the pen and by what they write draws attention to writing among people.

quranic_events.text_en: In the account of Maryam's guardianship, people cast their pens to decide which of them would take care of her.

chronological_position.note_en: The Quran does not say when the pen was made or where it comes in the order of creation.

location.note_en: The Quran does not say where the pen is.

misconceptions.text_en: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The pen of the first revelation and the oath at the start of Surat al-Qalam are not turned here into a statement about a cosmic Pen that wrote all things. The verses say God taught by the pen and swear by it; the further claim is not in these verses.

lessons.text_en: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The first revelation names the pen as a means of teaching, so learning and writing are shown as gifts from the Most Generous.

vocabulary.text_en: Qalam (plural aqlam) is a pen; yasturun means they write; allama means He taught; midad is ink.
